links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT literature-based answers on implant treatment planning versus best available evidence
links.effect: ChatGPT's original answers to all six questions were revised after higher-quality, timely studies were supplied, and the revisions often reversed the original conclusions (e.g., splinting, cantilevers, overdenture preference).
links.quote: ChatGPT has not demonstrated the ability to accurately cull the literature, stratify the rigor of the evidence, and extract accurate implications from the studies selected to deliver the best evidence-based answers to questions on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses.

links.outcome: Reliability of ChatGPT as a source for synthesizing literature for scholarly articles
links.effect: Rated on 4 indices (retrievable source, representative literature, accurate interpretation, conclusion reflects best evidence); concluded ChatGPT could not reliably synthesize the literature for the 6 questions.
links.quote: ChatGPT has not demonstrated the ability to accurately cull the literature, stratify the rigor of the evidence, and extract accurate implications from the studies selected to deliver the best evidence-based answers to questions on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT's baseline responses to dental implant treatment planning queries versus its revised answers after being provided with higher quality literature.

primary.practice: expert feedback with literature provision for revision
